canonicalRecord.title: plans:set-now / plans:set-status reject exact-slug calls with harness_required, while plans:get auto-resolves the same slug in the same session
canonicalRecord.summary:
Reproduced 2026-08-27T15:02Z from an su session scoped to workspace papercusp-workspace.

In ONE turn, same session, same exact plan slug 'own-tui-full-divorce-2026-08-24':
- plans:get { slug } -> ok, resolved harness 'papercusp' with no explicit harness arg.
- plans:get { slug, decisions:[...] } -> ok, same, no harness.
- plans:set-status { slug, item:'P-020', status:'wip', note } -> FAILED harness_required.
- plans:set-now { slug, state, next } -> FAILED harness_required (threw, flagged 'uncertain' by code:run, i.e. may-have-landed ambiguity on a write).
Retrying both with harness:'papercusp' succeeded unchanged.

The plans:get / plans:items tool docs state that an exact slug auto-resolves the owning harness within the caller's workspace. The write-side verbs do not honor that contract, and the refusal text does not say the read side behaves differently — so the natural read is that the session lost scope, not that the verb differs.

Two costs, the second worse than the first:
1. Every write-side plan call needs a retry an agent cannot predict from the read that just succeeded.
2. plans:set-now THREW rather than returning ok:false, so code:run classified it 'uncertain' with a may-have-landed warning on a WRITE. That forces a verify-before-retry round trip to avoid a double-write of the ## Now block.

Related but NOT a duplicate: EI-21581052016426676 (done) filed the same contract inconsistency for plans:get-item. This is the write-side pair (set-now / set-status), still live. The general fix is to make exact-slug harness auto-resolution uniform across the plans verbs, or to state the read/write asymmetry in the refusal message.

current.title: Indefinitely-paused pot still receives demand-floor wake injections — each burns a full Mug turn to re-confirm the pause and do nothing
current.summary:
OBSERVED (papercusp Mug, ≥4 consecutive wakes 2026-07-19 07:16→08:12): pot papercusp is owner-paused indefinitely (pauseNewWork:true, pausedUntil:null, directive:null, eligiblePlans:[]). Despite the pause, the platform keeps re-injecting demand-floor wakes on every work_items:create of an unplaced item, plus a watchdog boot wake on host reboot. Each wake spins up a full Mug model turn whose ONLY permitted action is to re-confirm the pause via pot:get-steering and declare mode:none — zero placement is allowed, so the turn is pure token burn.

WHY WASTEFUL: a paused Mug can take no placement action, so waking the model per new-demand-item during an INDEFINITE pause produces nothing but cost. Awareness of accrued demand is already delivered deterministically in the next legitimate wake's brief (pot:survey floor) — it does not need a live model turn per item.

PROPOSED DURABLE FIX: when a pot has pauseNewWork:true AND pausedUntil:null, suppress (or coalesce) demand-floor wake injections until the pause is lifted / a pausedUntil elapses. The accrued unplaced-demand count still surfaces in the next brief on unpause. Guard: unit test on the wake-injection path asserting a demand-floor injection is skipped while a pot is indefinitely paused.

DETECTOR ANGLE: the wake-reason text itself flags 'Frequent watchdog wakes are a prompt bug to fix' — this is that class, for the paused-pot case.

current.title: P-010: make dev:pipeline_position EMIT the state plane — stamp each volatile value with its cell id + a caller-relativity-correct re-read handle, derived from the registry
current.summary:
Last Phase 2 item of state-plane-adoption-2026-08-02. Tiers 1-3 (routing, guidance, nudges) are PROMOTION and promotion asymptotes at the measured 1.7% (D-030). P-010 makes the door emit the plane so adoption stops being a behaviour we promote.

SCOPED AGAINST THE TREE FIRST (the plan's own 9-for-10 standing lesson). Premise CONFIRMED, and stronger than filed:

- `gitPipelinePosition()` @ packages/operator-core/lib/git-pipeline-position.ts is real and IS the single resolver (the door's own header already claims axis-5 compliance).
- Better than the item's text assumed: the door<->cell map is ALREADY DECLARED DATA, not something to invent. Every cell carries `changeSignal: { kind:'poll', tool:'dev:pipeline_position', path:'<path in this very payload>' }`. So the stamp is DERIVED from the registry — no hand-written list, no drift, axis 5 preserved.
- 6 cells route through this door: git.pipelinePosition(positions.deployed), gate.greenCheckpoint.verdict(gate.consecutiveReds), gate.greenCheckpoint.candidate(changeInCandidate.judgingSha), gate.greenCheckpoint.ownership(gate.ownership.claimState), deploy.3070.sha(deployedSha), git.mainBehindStaging(verdictProvenance.mainFastForwarded).
- Prior art exists for SELECTING this set (cell-falsifier-reality.test.ts:133) but nothing EMITS it. P-010 is unbuilt.

TWO SHARP EDGES the item text does not mention, both of which decide whether the handle is correct or actively wrong:

1. CALLER-RELATIVITY. 2 of the 6 cells are `callerRelativity:{kind:'parameter',param:'path'}`. A re-read handle emitted WITHOUT `as:<the caller's path>` hands back a DIFFERENT answer than the value the caller is holding — a wrong handle is worse than no handle, because it looks authoritative. The handle must thread the caller's own `path` arg.
2. MISSING != NULL. The stamp must key on OWN-KEY EXISTENCE, not `valueAtPath`, which collapses a legitimately-null value into "absent". `deployedSha: null` is exactly the case where re-reading matters most; dropping its stamp there would make the feature vanish precisely when it is needed. cell-read.ts:503-515 and cell-falsifier-reality.test.ts:23 both already draw this line, but the existence walker (`pathExists`) lives ONLY in a test file — production has no such helper.

PLAN: new pure module state-plane-stamp.ts (payload + cells + callerPath -> stamps), hermetically testable, exporting the own-key-existence walker production currently lacks; door projects it additively as a `plane` block (non-breaking).

current.title: truncation-honesty registry: the `ambient-push-door` lossless exemption states a reason that is factually FALSE on two counts (borrow item 8 / P-007 measurement)
current.summary:
P-007 asked: MEASURE which door populations are head-relevant before making middle-elision (borrow item 8) a default anywhere. The measurement says middle elision earns NOTHING in any of the three live populations — but it surfaced a wrong claim in the truncation-honesty registry.

DOORS entry `ambient-push-door` (truncation-honesty-guard.test.ts:120-131) is registered `lossless` with the reason: "Overflow drops TAIL TEASERS only; the dropped candidates stay queued and re-deliver on the next pass, and every teaser is a pull-handle whose detail was never inline."

Both halves of that reason are false against the code:

(1) "the dropped candidates stay queued and re-deliver on the next pass" — FALSE for anything the DOOR cuts. ambient-push-delivery.ts calls recordDelivered(deliveredIds) at :236 for EVERY selected push, then renders at :240 and only then cuts at :286 (applyPushInjectionDoor). deliveredRefs feeds the novelty set (known.refs) and isNovelPush drops a known ref as 'not-novel', so a push cut by the door is marked delivered, never rendered into anyone's context, and suppressed on every later pass in the window. The re-delivery property belongs to selectPushes' `dropped` set (below-floor / severity-gated / budget-exhausted) — a DIFFERENT set from what the door cuts. The reason conflates the two.

(2) "drops TAIL TEASERS only" — FALSE since the P-012 auto-inject leg. `block` is teasers PLUS appended peer briefs (:264-281), so the tail region is briefs, not only teasers.

EXPOSURE (measured, not assumed): with PAPERCUSP_AMBIENT_CURSOR off (the default everywhere), the block cannot reach the door at all. Door budget = computeTurnDoors(0).injections = 8000*0.125 = 1000 tok = 4000 chars. Max block = 88-char header + at most DEFAULT_PUSH_POLICIES max budget (interactive = 6) lines, each <= TEASER_MAX_CHARS(200) + handle overhead — well under 4000. So the CONCLUSION (nothing unrecoverable is lost) currently holds, but for a reason nobody recorded, and the recorded reason would license a real silent drop the moment a budget or teaser cap moved.

FIX: correct the registry reason to the true one (teasers provably fit the door; only the flag-gated, re-pullable peer-brief tail is ever cuttable), and add a falsifiable bound test that constructs a worst-case block from the REAL constants and asserts the door does not cut it — so raising a push budget / teaser cap, or lowering the injections door, reds instead of silently converting the exemption into a silent drop.

DOORS entry `ambient-push-door` (truncation-honesty-guard.test.ts:120-131) is registered `lossless` with the reason: "Overflow drops TAIL TEASERS only; the dropped candidates stay queued and re-deliver on the next pass, and every teaser is a pull-handle whose detail was never inline."

Both halves of that reason are false against the code:

(1) "the dropped candidates stay queued and re-deliver on the next pass" — FALSE for anything the DOOR cuts. ambient-push-delivery.ts calls recordDelivered(deliveredIds) at :236 for EVERY selected push, then renders at :240 and only then cuts at :286 (applyPushInjectionDoor). deliveredRefs feeds the novelty set (known.refs) and isNovelPush drops a known ref as 'not-novel', so a push cut by the door is marked delivered, never rendered into anyone's context, and suppressed on every later pass in the window. The re-delivery property belongs to selectPushes' `dropped` set (below-floor / severity-gated / budget-exhausted) — a DIFFERENT set from what the door cuts. The reason conflates the two.

(2) "drops TAIL TEASERS only" — FALSE since the P-012 auto-inject leg. `block` is teasers PLUS appended peer briefs (:264-281), so the tail region is briefs, not only teasers.

EXPOSURE (measured, not assumed): with PAPERCUSP_AMBIENT_CURSOR off (the default everywhere), the block cannot reach the door at all. Door budget = computeTurnDoors(0).injections = 8000*0.125 = 1000 tok = 4000 chars. Max block = 88-char header + at most DEFAULT_PUSH_POLICIES max budget (interactive = 6) lines, each <= TEASER_MAX_CHARS(200) + handle overhead — well under 4000. So the CONCLUSION (nothing unrecoverable is lost) currently holds, but for a reason nobody recorded, and the recorded reason would license a real silent drop the moment a budget or teaser cap moved.

FIX: correct the registry reason to the true one (teasers provably fit the door; only the flag-gated, re-pullable peer-brief tail is ever cuttable), and add a falsifiable bound test that constructs a worst-case block from the REAL constants and asserts the door does not cut it — so raising a push budget / teaser cap, or lowering the injections door, reds instead of silently converting the exemption into a silent drop.

current.title: Prune the dead Mug/Kettle tier CSS in left-sidebar.styles.ts per-class — a range delete would break live UI because pc-queen__* is shared
current.summary:
Deliberately DEFERRED out of P-063 (see D-096 and the P-063 section of _retired/mug-kettle-deciders/RESTORE.md, edit #6). Filed rather than dropped.

WHAT IS DEAD. P-063 retired MugTab + MugHeartbeat + ModelTiersOverride + ThrottleSection + AutonomySurfacing (2026-08-12), and the earlier P-059/D-083 slice retired OverwatchTab. Their CSS all stayed in apps/operator-vite/src/components/left-sidebar/left-sidebar.styles.ts, in five section blocks that were at (pre-change) :857 OverwatchTab · :937 MugTab+MugHeartbeat+ModelTiersOverride · :1023 MugHeartbeat · :1050 ModelTiersOverride · :1075 ThrottleSection+AutonomySurfacing — a contiguous-looking ~275-line span ending just before :1132 (AccountsTab).

WHY IT IS NOT A RANGE DELETE, measured 2026-08-12. The `pc-queen__*` class family inside that span is SHARED with components that SURVIVE: apps/operator-vite/src/components/left-sidebar/{PotSteeringTree,RailSection,PapercupTab,AutomationPane}.tsx (+ AutomationPane.test.tsx) and libs/generic/ui-primitives/src/override/{OverridableSetting.tsx,override.styles.ts}. Deleting the range would strip live rules and produce a visual regression in surviving panels — including a GENERIC borrowable lib, so the blast radius is not even confined to this app.

The prefixes that ARE provably unused by live code (grep over apps/packages/libs excluding _retired/, 2026-08-12): pc-overwatch, pc-throttle, pc-autonomy, pc-tiers, pc-heartbeat — each returned NONE. But those rules are INTERLEAVED with the shared pc-queen__* ones inside the same blocks, so the work is per-class, not per-block.

HOW TO DO IT SAFELY. Enumerate every selector in the span; for each, grep the live tree (excluding _retired/) for the bare class name; delete only selectors with zero live references. Beware two traps this plan has hit repeatedly: (a) a shared NAME does not imply a shared verdict — the pc-queen__ prefix is exactly that trap, so match whole class names, not prefixes; (b) `.pc-queen__section-title` is referenced from a COMMENT in the AccountsTab region (~:1504), which is prose, not a use — do not let a comment hit save a genuinely dead rule, and do not let its absence condemn a live one.

WHY IT IS LOW URGENCY. Dead CSS is inert — it ships bytes and nothing else. A deleted shared class is a live visual regression. That asymmetry is the whole reason this was split out of the retirement slice rather than rushed inside it.

VERIFY: npm run test:affected, plus a REAL Tauri-shell check of the left sidebar (Accounts / Papercup / Agents / System / Spend tabs and the automation pane) per /internal/docs/testing/agent-e2e — jsdom does not compute styles, so a CSS regression is invisible to it.
